title: Record the model budget instead of overwriting it
ask: hq/data/outbox/_limit.json holds one limit event and is overwritten by the next, so the studio's largest recurring cost has no history whatsoever. Append each event to hq/data/history/limits.jsonl instead — hit at, reset at, and how many requests were parked — beside the run and deploy histories that already work this way. It is a few lines, and it is the difference between Finance reporting a $2.23 art spend and Finance reporting what this studio actually costs to run.
first_action: Read note_limit and _save_limit_locked in hq/server.py, and the append_history helper beside them.
source_message: hq/data/outbox/_limit.json holds one limit event and is overwritten by the next, so the studio's largest recurring cost has no history whatsoever. Append each event to hq/data/history/limits.jsonl instead — hit at, reset at, and how many requests were parked — beside the run and deploy histories that already work this way. result: Executed by a Sonnet worker holding only Harold's seat context; verified by the chief of staff. note_limit appends {event: hit, until} once per fresh outage (debounced — retries while limited write nothing) and clear_limit appends {event: clear, parked} with the queue depth, to hq/data/history/limits.jsonl via the same append_history the run history uses. Proven in a sandboxed run of the real functions. The worker also caught a false premise in the card: deploy history did NOT already append as claimed — the chief of staff closed that in the same change (_run_deploy's terminal state now appends to history/deploys.jsonl).
